engines.name: 4.4L twin-turbo V8 mild hybrid (M60i and X6 M)

issues.t: V8 timing chain and guide wear
issues.sym: A rattle on cold start that fades as the engine warms, then timing-related check engine codes. Left alone, the chain can jump and badly damage the engine.
issues.why: The twin-turbo V8 puts its turbos inside the V, which cooks the oil and the plastic chain guides. Guides wear and the chain stretches, faster with long oil change intervals. BMW's N63 Customer Care Package addressed early engines.
issues.next: Have a BMW specialist inspect the chain around 80,000 miles or at any cold-start rattle. Ask a dealer whether the Customer Care Package was done on your VIN, and change the oil about every 5,000–7,500 miles.

issues.t: V8 burns oil and smokes on startup
issues.sym: Blue-gray smoke from the exhaust right after starting, especially after the car sits overnight, low oil warnings between services, and a burning oil smell.
issues.why: Extreme heat in the V8 hardens the valve stem seals and wears piston rings, and faulty crankcase vent parts add to it. Burning about a quart every 1,000–1,500 miles is common on higher-mileage engines.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and keep it topped up. Have a shop confirm the cause; valve stem seals are the usual fix, but a worn engine may need more.

issues.t: Auxiliary water pump can overheat and start a fire (recalls)
issues.sym: Often no warning. Some owners notice a burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, even with the car off.
issues.why: The circuit board in the electric auxiliary water pump that cools the turbochargers can overheat and smolder.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 11V-521 and 18V-248 and get the free pump replacement. Until then, park outdoors and away from buildings.

issues.t: Passenger front airbag inflator can rupture (recalls)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: Takata-type passenger airbag inflators break down with heat and humidity and can burst in a crash, spraying metal fragments. NHTSA lists several of these as do-not-drive recalls.
issues.next: Run your VIN through the recall lookup now. If recall 16V-364, 17V-020, 18V-030, 19V-017 or 20V-016 is open, do not drive the car until the free repair is done.

issues.t: Driver front airbag inflator can rupture (recalls)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: The driver airbag inflator, including some interim replacement inflators, can degrade and burst in a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 16V-071 and 20V-017 and get the free airbag replacement right away.

issues.t: Transfer case and actuator wear
issues.sym: 4WD or xDrive warning light, a whir or grind under load, and binding or hesitation in tight, slow turns.
issues.why: The all-wheel-drive transfer case's clutch pack wears and its small actuator motor fails with mileage. Mismatched tire sizes or worn tires make it worse.
issues.next: Have the transfer case fluid and actuator checked first. An actuator alone costs far less than a new transfer case, so get a second opinion before a full replacement.

issues.t: Fuel pump wiring can fail and leak fuel (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or will not start, or you smell fuel.
issues.why: The wire contacts inside the in-tank fuel pump module may not be crimped well enough, which can cut power to the pump or let fuel leak.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-746 and get the free fuel pump module replacement.

issues.t: Rear brake discs may break (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding, vibration or a change in braking feel from the rear.
issues.why: Some rear brake discs did not meet BMW's specifications and could crack, reducing braking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 09V-255 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Front driveshaft joint can fail (recalls)
issues.sym: A clunk or vibration from under the front of the car, or a sudden loss of drive to the front wheels.
issues.why: The universal joint on the front driveshaft may not seal out water and dirt, so it corrodes and fails.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 16V-311 and 17V-138 and get the free driveshaft replacement.

issues.t: Power steering fluid can leak onto the exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the engine bay, or power steering fluid leaking.
issues.why: A machining error on the steering gear can let power steering fluid leak onto hot exhaust parts, which can start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 12V-267 and get the free repair done.

issues.t: Turbo charge pipe cracks
issues.sym: A sudden loss of power, a loud whoosh or hiss when you accelerate, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The plastic pipe that carries boosted air from the turbo to the intercooler gets brittle and splits, more often in cold weather.
issues.next: Have the pipe inspected for cracks. It is a fairly simple swap, and aluminum replacements are available.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the valve cover gasket
issues.sym: A burning oil smell, light smoke from the engine bay, or oil on the spark plugs. The low oil warning may come on.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket hardens with heat and leaks oil, often onto the hot exhaust. On the B58 the plastic cover with its built-in crankcase vent valve can also crack or its valve can fail.
issues.next: Get the leak fixed soon, since oil on the exhaust is a fire risk. On the B58, ask whether the whole valve cover should be replaced.

issues.t: Electric water pump or thermostat fails
issues.sym: A coolant temperature or engine warning light, sometimes followed by overheating and reduced power.
issues.why: The electric water pump and the plastic thermostat housing are common failure points on the six-cylinder engine.
issues.next: If the temperature warning comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Replace the pump and thermostat together.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel pump wear
issues.sym: Rough idle, misfires, hard starting, or a ticking or rattling from the top of the engine at idle.
issues.why: The high-pressure pump that feeds the direct injectors wears early on these engines.
issues.next: Have the fuel pressure checked with a scan tool before replacing parts. Some engine codes look similar.

issues.t: Coolant hoses and expansion tank crack
issues.sym: Sudden coolant loss, low coolant warnings, a sweet smell, or the temperature climbing.
issues.why: Plastic coolant parts, including the expansion tank, hoses and cap, crack under heat, especially on the hot-running V8 and with big temperature swings.
issues.next: Do not keep driving if the temperature warning comes on. Have the system pressure-tested to find the cracked part.

issues.t: Turbo oil feed lines leak
issues.sym: Light smoke when slowing down, or an oil smell from the engine bay.
issues.why: Heat from the turbos sitting inside the V8 breaks down the oil lines and their seals where they join the block.
issues.next: Have the turbo oil lines inspected and resealed. Use quality oil and keep changes frequent to protect the turbo bearings.

issues.t: X6 M connecting rod bearing wear
issues.sym: Often no warning until a knocking noise from the bottom of the engine or a low oil pressure warning.
issues.why: The connecting rod bearings in the high-output V8 wear quickly on cars that are driven hard or tracked.
issues.next: Use the correct oil and change it often. Owners of hard-driven cars often replace the bearings around 60,000 miles as prevention.

issues.t: Front control arm bushing wear
issues.sym: A knock or clunk from the front over bumps and vague, wandering steering.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms wear out on this heavy SUV, typically around 50,000–80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked for play and get an alignment after the repair.

issues.t: Air suspension compressor or strut failure
issues.sym: The car sits low at one corner or the rear, the compressor runs a lot, or a suspension warning appears.
issues.why: The air struts' rubber bags leak with age and the compressor wears out from running to make up for the leaks.
issues.next: Have the system tested for leaks before replacing the compressor, or the new one will fail too.

issues.t: Rear child seat anchors can be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms unless you notice bent lower anchor bars.
issues.why: Rigid-style child seat connectors can damage the rear lower anchor bars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-823 and get the free reinforcing bracket installed.

issues.t: Suspension bolts may be loose or too soft (recalls)
issues.sym: Clunking from the suspension, or in the worst case a control arm breaking and a loss of control.
issues.why: Some front suspension bolts were not tightened properly, and some control arm pivot bolts were not hardened correctly and can break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 17V-727, 18V-439 and 18V-680 and get the free repair right away.

issues.t: Wheel bolts may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clicking or knocking from a wheel, or vibration.
issues.why: The wheel bolts may not have been tightened properly and can loosen or break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-614. If a wheel feels loose or noisy, stop and have it checked.

issues.t: Starter can overheat and start a fire (recalls)
issues.sym: The engine is slow to start or will not crank after several tries, or there is a burning smell.
issues.why: The starter motor can overheat during repeated start attempts. Owners also report starter failures around 50,000 miles.
issues.next: Do not keep cranking if it will not start. Check your VIN for recalls 24V-576 and 25V-644.

issues.t: Rear spoiler can come off (recalls)
issues.sym: Wind noise or movement from the rear spoiler.
issues.why: The rear spoiler may not be bonded properly to its mounting plate and can detach while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 20V-095 and 20V-484 and get the free inspection.

issues.t: Brake unit rotor and shaft can separate (recall)
issues.sym: Brake and ABS warnings and reduced brake assist, especially after hard braking.
issues.why: Inside the integrated brake unit, a rotor and shaft can separate during hard braking, cutting ABS and brake assist.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-062 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Backup camera view can be blocked or blank (recalls)
issues.sym: The rear camera image is partly hidden or the screen does not show it in reverse.
issues.why: A software issue with the camera display settings.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 19V-684 and 21V-096 and get the free software update.

issues.t: Front axle bracket weld can separate (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front right or the car pulling to one side.
issues.why: The weld between the front axle carrier and the right front control arm bracket may not be strong enough.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-678 and get the free inspection.

issues.t: Sunroof can close without the key (recall)
issues.sym: The sunroof may close even when the key fob is not in the car.
issues.why: The roof control unit was programmed incorrectly, which can let it close without the key and pinch someone.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 22V-267 and get the free reprogramming.

issues.t: 48-volt battery cable connection can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, warning lights, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: The connection between the 48-volt mild-hybrid battery and the starter-generator may have high resistance and get hot.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-761 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Steering column joint bolt may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or play in the steering.
issues.why: The bolt on the steering shaft universal joint may not have been tightened to spec and can work loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-031 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Transmission control unit can leak and lock a gear (recall)
issues.sym: A transmission warning, the car stuck in one gear, or a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.why: Transmission fluid can seep past a faulty weld into the transmission control unit and damage it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-821 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Knee airbags may not deploy properly (recalls)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash.
issues.why: Some driver and passenger knee airbags were built incorrectly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-471 and 23V-622 and get the free repair.

issues.t: Integrated brake system can lose power assist (recalls)
issues.sym: Brake and stability control warnings, a hard pedal, and longer stopping distances.
issues.why: The integrated brake unit can malfunction and lose power assist and ABS/stability control. Owners filed several complaints, and BMW has issued follow-up campaigns.
issues.next: If brake warnings appear, drive gently to a dealer or tow it. Check your VIN for recalls 24V-104, 24V-739, 24V-697 and 26V-422.

issues.t: Seat belt sensor may not detect an unbelted occupant (recall)
issues.sym: The seat belt reminder may not work correctly.
issues.why: Front seat belt sensing may fail, and the airbags may not deploy as intended.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-345 and get the free repair.
